images.title: Drawing a fraction length
images.purpose: Give the method cue for drawing a fraction length: cut 0 to 1 into as many equal parts as the bottom number, then draw from 0 over as many parts as the top number, shown with 3/4.
images.composition: One worked number line in the middle of the frame and one short task line centred above it, with plenty of white space.
images.exact_structure: A grey #6B7280 number line from 0 to 1 only, drawn long, with exactly 5 evenly spaced ticks making 4 equal parts. A thick teal #0072B2 line runs from 0 to the 3rd tick after 0, with the label 3/4 above its end. Exactly 3 small equal amber #E69F00 arcs over the 3 parts the teal line covers. Centred above everything, the task text in reddish purple #CC79A7. Exactly 1 number line, 1 teal line, 3 arcs.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any line, tick or mark drawn for the task lengths
images.takeaway: The bottom number tells how many equal parts; the top number tells how many to count from 0.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 1 cut into 4 equal parts with a teal line over 3 parts labelled 3/4 as a sample; the task to draw the three given lengths sits above.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how many equal parts each task length needs before drawing it.

image_decisions.why: A sample length drawn on a cut unit shows the method without drawing the task lengths.
